CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency Region of Nunukan.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

REGENT OF NUNUKAN

PROVINCE OF NORTH KALIMANTAN

REGIONAL REGULATION OF NUNUKAN REGENCY

NUMBER 17 OF 2015

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF NUNUKAN,

Considering:
Bearing in Mind:
a. that the right of every citizen to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence;
b. that all forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination;
c. that laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region so that institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation;
d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Nunukan Regency concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children;
1.

Article 51

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and child victims of violence is conducted at the end of each Budget year or if necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the health field as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;

b exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically exploited, sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.

3. Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

Article 33

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; andb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Part Four

Prevention of Violence against Women and Children

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 50

1. To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by Technical SKPD and PPT.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.
4. Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of SKPD implementing policies and activities for the protection of Women and child victims of violence.
5. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

CHAPTER X

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 54

1. In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community may:a. form family partners at the Village/Kelurahan level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims; andd. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and/or mass media.

Article 28

Physical violence as referred to in Article 27 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

1. Region is the Regency Region of Nunukan.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

Article 54

1. In the implementation of Protection of Women and children, the community may:a. form family partners at the Village/Kelurahan level by the community;
b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims; andd. report to the competent authority if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by individuals, community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and/or mass media.

Article 5

1. In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, women must be empowered.
2. Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in economic, socio-cultural, political, and legal activities.

Article 6

1. The Regional Government is obliged and responsible in efforts to empower women.
2. Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF NUNUKAN,

Considering:
Bearing in Mind:
a. that the right of every citizen to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence;
b. that all forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination;
c. that laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region so that institutional support and regulations are needed to ensure its implementation;
d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Nunukan Regency concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children;
1.

Article 43

1. Social reintegration services as referred to in Article 37 letter f aim to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with: a. relevant government and non-government agencies and institutions; andb. village community institutions and/or local community leaders.

Article 10

1. The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) includes: a enhancement of awareness and knowledge in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and b facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
2. The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 16

1. The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the health field as referred to in Article 13 letter b, the Regional Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb which is carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity and supported by community participation.
2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;

b exemption from cost burdens for malnourished children, children undergoing dialysis due to kidney failure, children with thalassemia major, children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically exploited, sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.

3. Children as referred to in paragraph (2) are children from poor families except as otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

Article 15

The Implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of birth registration, as referred to in Article 13 letter a, the Regional Government is obliged to organize the registration of children's births with the issuance of birth certificates in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

1. Region is the Regency Region of Nunukan.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the implementation of Government Affairs which are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Work Unit hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

Article 33

Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence include: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; andb. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CONCERNING

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF NUNUKAN,

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency Region of Nunukan.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of Nunukan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Nunukan.

5. Technical Regional Work Unit hereinafter referred to as technical SKPD is a Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Nunukan Regency area.
12. Protection is all preventive, service and empowerment actions to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.
